Update roxygen2 documentation with newly added variables

Source: R/update.R
sd_update_roxygen.Rd

Surveys and other research datasets often grow new variables over time – computed sum scores, a new wave's questions, and so on. Regenerating the whole roxygen2 block with sd_generate_roxygen() every time would throw away any text you already reviewed and approved. sd_update_roxygen() instead only asks the language model to describe the NEW variables, and inserts them into the existing \describe{} block, leaving the title, description, @details, @source, and all previously documented variables untouched. The @format line's variable count is corrected automatically (never left to the model).

Usage

sd_update_roxygen(
  x,
  object_name,
  file = NULL,
  new_vars = NULL,
  model = "gemma3:12b",
  backend = "ollama",
  language = "fi",
  timeout_s = 1200,
  dry_run = TRUE
)

Arguments

x

An sd_data object containing the CURRENT, full set of variables (old and new).

object_name

Name the documented object has, e.g. "survey_data" – the same name used with sd_generate_roxygen().

file

Path to the existing roxygen2 file to update. Defaults to file.path("R", paste0(object_name, ".R")).

new_vars

Character vector of variable names to describe. NULL (the default) auto-detects them by comparing x against what is already documented in file.

model, backend, timeout_s

As in sd_document().

language

Language the new variable descriptions should be written in – one of "fi" (Finnish, the default), "en" (English) or "sv" (Swedish). Should normally match the language file was already written in. See sd_build_prompt().

dry_run

If TRUE (the default), the updated text is only returned, not written to disk. Set to FALSE to write it to file (a .bak backup of the previous version is made first).

Value

An object of class sd_roxygen_update with elements text (the full updated file content), added_vars (character vector of variables that were newly documented – empty if none were found), file, backup_file (path to the .bak copy, or NULL when dry_run = TRUE or nothing changed), prompt, model, backend, chat, and created.

Details

New variables are found automatically by parsing which variables are already documented in file and comparing them to names(x$data) – the same idea sd_check_documentation_current() uses. If that parsing is uncertain (e.g. a heavily hand-edited file) or you simply know which variables you want described, pass new_vars explicitly instead.

By default (dry_run = TRUE) nothing is written to disk. Set dry_run = FALSE to write the update; the previous version of file is always copied to <file>.bak first, so an unwanted update can be undone by restoring that copy.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# aineisto sisältää nyt esim. uuden summamuuttujan "tt_mean":
tulos <- sd_update_roxygen(aineisto, "survey_data")
print(tulos)   # tarkista lisätyt kuvaukset ennen tallennusta
sd_update_roxygen(aineisto, "survey_data", dry_run = FALSE)
} # }
